name: Idiopathic Chronic Pancreatitis

criteria.description: Recurrent or chronic abdominal pain consistent with pancreatitis
Imaging findings of pancreatic ductal irregularities, calcifications, or atrophy on CT/MRI/ERCP
Evidence of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency such as steatorrhea or abnormal fecal elastase
Exclusion of other known causes of chronic pancreatitis including alcohol, genetic mutations, autoimmune pancreatitis, and obstructive etiologies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic pancreatic-type abdominal pain, characteristic imaging findings, and exclusion of other known causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging and exclusion of secondary causes.

common.symptomName: Steatorrhea due to exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
Diabetes mellitus secondary to endocrine insufficiency

laboratory: Low fecal elastase indicating exocrine insufficiency
Elevated serum glucose in cases with diabetes
Mildly elevated serum amylase and lipase during acute exacerbations
imaging: Pancreatic ductal irregularities and strictures on MRCP or ERCP
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified in idiopathic cases
other: Exclusion of alcohol use and autoimmune markers

distinguishingFeatures: More common in males with alcohol abuse history
Similar imaging but with identifiable cause
Characteristic imaging with diffuse pancreatic enlargement
Earlier onset in childhood or adolescence

redFlags: Sudden worsening of abdominal pain with signs of acute pancreatitis
Development of jaundice or biliary obstruction
references: Yadav D, Lowenfels AB. The epidemiology of pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer. Gastroenterology. 2013 Jun;144(6):1252-61.
Whitcomb DC. Clinical practice. Acute pancreatitis. N Engl J Med. 2006 May 11;354(20):2142-50.
Forsmark CE. Management of chronic pancreatitis. Gastroenterology. 2013 May;144(6):1282-91.
